chapter: Day jobs and later Billy and De De engagements
title: Playing at Lutton's and the Silver Star with Billy and De De
summary: Lewis recalls long stretches at Lutton's and the Silver Star, where the owners drank heavily. Another job with Frankie Gibbs is mentioned.

bands.name: Billie and De De Pierce's band

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: More than you huh? Mm-mm. Oh, you ever work at Lutton's? Oh yeah. Sure. I worked at Lutton's, I worked there with Bill and the D and M too. I worked there a long while.

I put Big Guy Louie there. I put Rogers, Ernest Rogers there. I worked there a long while. I worked there a long while. I worked with them at the Silver Store at St. Claude and St. Bernard. St. But there stuff I worked there a long while. I worked with them at the Silver Star at St. Claude and St. Bernard. I worked there with them a long while. But they were terrible people. They were terrible.
You told me once how much he could drink on a job. How many cases of beer could he drink?
He drank two or three cases of beer a night. That's a fact. That's the truth. I'm not joking. I'm not going to tell you where to lie. She would drink.
At night, I worked with them in Bunky, and they would, we'd soon walk in and the man would pay it off. And he'd order two case of beer, and she'd order a gallon of sherry wine.
Who was up there in Bunky?
Myself, and it was a very good tramo player, I can't call his name now, but I know he's
Frankie Gibbs. Frankie Gibbs. He was a cripple.
